Exhibit C TENANT DESIGN CRITERIA | Nashville Farmers Market MARKET DESIGN CONCEPT The Nashville Farmers Market has remodeled the interior of the Market’s main building. This project will require all merchants to submit design packages that conform to the following rules. Each Tenant Design package will be reviewed by the Market Board of Directors, the Market Director and where necessary, the State of Tennessee. In addition, the Tenant’s plans must be approved by all the required agencies that review plans in Davidson County. Each shop will be reviewed both independently and how it interacts with the shops surrounding it. Tenants are encouraged to develop bold and creative shop designs within a set framework that ensures a lively, almost entertaining atmosphere, but within the overall design of the Market. Shops should allow open and clear contact between the merchant and customer and generous and attractive display of all products. Designs that feature the production of a specific product are encouraged. Much of the visual excitement of the Market depends on the openness of each stand allowing simultaneous intimate and long views of the Market as a whole. Each shop must be laid out so that it is both an attractive statement in itself, but also a window that provides views to the Market that lay beyond that particular shop. The Markets goal is the effective display of the full range of merchandise, without clutter and confusion, while maintaining easy but secure access for both customer and merchant. The character of each shop should reinforce the basic product group it offers. A good design allows the merchandise to speak for itself, with customer sight-lines to product production if possible. This will increase the customer’s interest in the merchant’s product and a sense of excitement. Only durable design and materials which will hold up under the usage experienced over the long term will be approved. Like any business investment, the shop should be seen as a capital asset that will retain its value only when planned and properly maintained. The optimum balance in the Market derives from individual shops that provide unity to the site as a whole while remaining unique in themselves. Compatibility with adjacent counters, signage and presentation must be taken into consideration and will be reviewed during the approval process. Codes Conditions Tenant design, construction, and operation shall comply with governing federal, state, and local codes regulations — including but not limited to egress, health, handicap-accessibility, plumbing, mechanical, electrical, and fire-suppression. Tenants shall be responsible for submittal of professional engineered design documents to applicable State and Metro Codes authorities in order to obtain building permits. This list is provided only as a convenient reference; Tenants shall be responsible for confirming applicable Codes regulations as well as review/inspection authorities. Architectural “trellis”: An overhead “trellis” frame is intended to be utilized for distribution of water piping and power conduit in open areas. (See Market standard drawings.) Tenant partitions: Wood or metal stud with gypsum wallboard, 12 feet high maximum. Architectural finishes: Materials within food preparation areas shall be impervious and scrubbable. Paint and stain shall be low-VOC formula. Any ceilings (optional) shall be subject to Market approval. Structural considerations: Kitchen cooking exhaust hoods and make-up air units must be supported by an independent frame that transfers weight to the overhead “trellis” or the floor slab. (Metro Water Services may require a supplemental Tenant backflow-preventer under special conditions.) Water heaters shall be electric except where gas is acceptable to the Market. Placement of exterior condensers-compressors for food-service equipment is subject to Market approval. Cooking hoods: Design and construction shall comply with currently-enforced editions of NFPA 96 and SMC Chapter 5 (a checklist for which is available from the Tennessee Fire Marshal’s office), as well as Market standard hood specifications. Placement of cooking hoods and conditioned makeup-air equipment, and routing of exhaust ductwork shall be controlled as shown on Market standard drawings. Fire detection and suppression: Cooking hoods shall be connected to building fire-alarm system as directed by the Market. The following four Design Zones (measured vertically from the floor) have been established: Lower Display Zone (from the floor to 42” above the floor / with specific approval up to 56” above the floor): All approved display fixtures and equipment are allowed. Public aisle frontage must be used for product display or service activity, except for access openings. Goods within display cases should be maintained as presentation instead of storage. Sewer: Non-grease-collecting sinks and floor drains may be tied directly into building sanitary line. Sinks in interior zones must be special self-venting type. Prior to final approval of electrical installation, Tenant shall notify Landlord who will then have a electrical meter installed. Lighting Tenant space illumination levels are subject to Market approval. Light sources generating glare in the common area are not allowed; provide special baffles or diffusers to shield lamps from direct view at eye- level.
